newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican cops jailed in death of U.S. tourists.
newsitem.headline: Mexican cops jailed in death of U.S. tourists.

text.p: Three policemen from the northern Mexican border city of Tijuana were jailed on Thursday in connection with the kidnapping and murder of two U.S. tourists, officials said.

The two tourists, Ramon Santillan and Juan Solorzano, both of Los Angeles, were abducted July 15 and later shot in the neck and buried in a Tijuana neighbourhood, prosecutors told a news conference, the government news agency Notimex reported.
Tijuana, a gateway to the United States, is across the border from San Diego. Tijuana is a major tourist destination for Americans and one of the more prosperous cities in Mexico.
But the city is also known for its high levels of police corruption and violence due to the narcotics trade and illegal immigration.
Agents of the Judicial Police in Baja California state arrested the three Tijuana municipal police officers, according to Ramon Anguis, a top official in the state prosecutor's office, Notimex said.
Anguis said four other people not on the police force also participated in the abduction.
The victims were killed and buried in the Herrera neighbourhood of Tijuana after their families failed to pay a ransom demanded by the kidnappers, Anguis said.
